```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(fgls)
```

Section S-4 of the Supplement to Perron and González-Coya (2026) combines the
two corrections:

* **F-C** corrects for serial correlation: Durbin regression, BIC lag selection,
  quasi-differencing;
* **F-CH** then models the variance of the filtered residuals with the adaptive
  Lasso of González-Coya and Perron (2024). The candidate covariates are built
  from the *unfiltered* regressors (or supplied in `z`), and the
  quasi-differenced regression is re-estimated by weighted least squares.

The variance of F-CH is the bias-corrected sandwich of the 2024 paper applied to
the filtered regressors (Supplement eqs. A.4--A.5). F-C intervals are built the
same way with unit weights.

```{r example}
sim <- simulate_combined(200, ar = c(1.34, -0.42), skedastic = "exp", seed = 5)
fit <- fgls(y ~ x, data = sim, seed = 1)
summary(fit)
compare_fgls(OLS = lm(y ~ x, data = sim), `F-C` = fit$stages$serial, `F-CH` = fit)
```

`fgls()` is the general function; this combined estimator is its default.

## The first-stage correction

The Supplement does not write out the correction for the estimated AR filter
that eq. (29) of the paper provides in the serial-only case. `fgls` adds the
heteroskedasticity-robust analogue of that term by default when the regressors
are declared pre-determined (`first_stage_correction = TRUE`, the default for
`exog = "predetermined"`). With exogenous regressors it is negligible. With
non-exogenous ones, simulations show that it is needed for correct coverage
(`vignette("validation")`).

```{r first-stage}
sim_ne <- simulate_combined(300, ar = 0.8, skedastic = "x2", gamma = 1, seed = 6)
with_fs <- fgls(y ~ x, data = sim_ne, seed = 1)
without_fs <- fgls(y ~ x, data = sim_ne, seed = 1, first_stage_correction = FALSE)
c(with = sqrt(vcov(with_fs)[2, 2]), without = sqrt(vcov(without_fs)[2, 2]))
```

## No loss under homoskedasticity

When the innovations are homoskedastic the Lasso typically selects nothing and
F-CH equals F-C:

```{r homo}
hom <- simulate_combined(200, ar = 0.5, skedastic = "homoskedastic", seed = 7)
fit_h <- fgls(y ~ x, data = hom, seed = 1)
fit_h$skedastic$selected
all.equal(coef(fit_h), coef(fit_h$stages$serial))
```

## Bootstrap cross-check

`vcov = "bootstrap"` re-runs the whole estimator on residual-based sieve
bootstrap samples, using the estimated AR filter with wild innovations. It is
an independent check of the analytic variance. The regressors are held fixed,
so with non-exogenous regressors it does not reproduce their feedback.

```{r bootstrap}
fb <- fgls(y ~ x, data = sim, seed = 1, vcov = "bootstrap", control = fgls_control(n_boot = 19))
cbind(analytic = sqrt(diag(vcov(fit))), bootstrap = sqrt(diag(vcov(fb))))
```
